findings.reason: Massachusetts state law bars cities and towns from enacting, maintaining or enforcing rent control. The only exception is a narrow local-option regime under this chapter. Under it, owner compliance becomes voluntary after six months. It cannot regulate evictions or apply to owners of fewer than ten units or to units with fair market rent over $400. The municipality must also compensate owners for the gap between market and controlled rent. As a result, no state or local rent increase cap applies in Massachusetts under this provision.

findings.reason: New Jersey has no statewide rent control law; rent control exists only through municipal ordinances. Qualified: related enacted rules exist at this level: NJ-RENT-01 (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1): no numeric cap; increase must not be unconscionable; NJ-RENT-02 (N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.5): 30 years after completion of construction.
findings.quoted_span: The State of New Jersey has no laws that establish, govern or control rents.
